svg.text: Admitting a cluster — reserve the whole window, then let the followers fall in
cluster_dim = (3,1,1). Only the FIRST member does any cluster reasoning; the other two are admitted by the ordinary standalone path.
VX_kmu — grid walk
admission logic
slot_valid_r / tail_r
warps of the cluster
LMEM
CTA A — is_first_of_cluster = 1, cluster_size = 3
cluster_k = clamp(3, 1, usable_slots_r)
base_slot = prewrap ? 0 : base_tail
the clamp is why an oversized cluster degrades, not deadlocks
test the WHOLE window: (slot_valid_r & cluster_window) == 0
alt window NOT free
admit_ok = 0 → kmu_bus_if.ready = 0
back-pressure — the KMU holds CTA A on the wire, `valid` stays high
The walk does not advance, so no member of this
cluster is emitted early. The cluster is admitted
atomically or not at all — there is no partial state
to unwind.
else window free — admit
admit_ok = 1
slot_valid_r[base_slot] <= 1
tail_r <= next_tail
only slot base_slot is claimed — NOT the window
The window is a TEST, not a claim
Nothing marks the other K−1 slots as reserved. They stay free in
slot_valid_r, and what protects them is simply that no other CTA
can reach this dispatcher before the followers do — the bus is in
order and the walk emits them next.
CTA B — is_first_of_cluster = 0
admit_ok = ~slot_valid_r[base_slot]
the plain standalone test — no cluster logic at all
claim base_slot = s0+1 (guaranteed free by A’s window test)
CTA C — is_first_of_cluster = 0
claim base_slot = s0+2
The cluster is now resident: slots s0, s0+1, s0+2
member r LMEM base = (s0 + r) * stride = issuer_base + r * stride
get_cluster_rank() = CTA_ID % CTA_CLUSTER_SIZE — the rank is derived, never sent
rank 0 issues one DXA multicast
the SMEM writer resolves each receiver as base + r · smem_stride
no per-slot base table, no receiver-side translation — the stride arithmetic is exact
This is the entire point of clustering
Without it, all K CTAs load the same operand independently — K fetches of the same
bytes. With it, rank 0 fetches once and multicasts to its K−1 peers in lockstep, at
the same SMEM offset, because their LMEM bases are a known stride apart.
The ordering this rests on — and what enforces it
Read the sequence again with one question in mind: what guarantees CTA B reaches the SAME dispatcher as CTA A? Nothing in the dispatcher does. The window test at
A’s admission proves the slots are free on THIS core, and B’s standalone test then finds slot s0+1 free — but only if B was routed here at all.
The LAUNCH BUS is what routes it here. A compute message is one CLUSTER: VX_kmu marks `eop` on the last member, and every arb level locks its input→output pair
from the first beat to `eop`. So A picks a ready core and B and C are delivered to that same core — clusters, not CTAs, are what round-robin across the machine.
cluster_dim (1,1,1), the default, marks every CTA `eop` and the lock never engages: the plain per-CTA round-robin, bit for bit. Same mechanism as fragment affinity.
